subject.title: feat(browser): send pages to OpenClaw from the Chrome extension

question: Should OpenClaw accept this official Chrome-extension page-sharing capability and its new plugin-SDK export once the default lazy-service delivery path is repaired?
rationale: The patch adds a user-facing browser-to-agent ingress path and expands the plugin SDK; the protected `maintainer` label indicates that product and API ownership should be explicit rather than inferred from implementation quality.

options.title: Sponsor after lifecycle repair
options.body: Keep the feature in core, move sink registration to the lazy Gateway lifecycle, and require default-path live proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the feature
options.body: Retain only an explicitly supported relay topology and remove or avoid the new public SDK surface if a smaller owner-boundary design is preferred.

options.title: Defer browser sharing
options.body: Pause the feature until maintainers choose the permanent browser-to-agent ingestion and plugin-SDK contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after lifecycle repair
recommendation.body: Keep the feature in core, move sink registration to the lazy Gateway lifecycle, and require default-path live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature history shows this contributor owns the branch’s relay, capture, and service-lifecycle implementation; broader merged-history ownership was not established in the supplied evidence.
